memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'From wherever you live, bring two loaves made of two-tenths of an
ephah of the finest flour, baked with yeast, as a wave offering of
firstfruits to the LORD'" - Lev 23:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is unusual. Yeast was normally excluded from offerings, yet here
God specifically commands two loaves baked with yeast.

We should be careful not to over-read symbolism the text does not
state. But one honest observation stands: unlike the spotless
sacrifices, these loaves are ordinary bread, made the way people
actually baked at home. They represent the people themselves,
presented to God - not a perfect animal, but real households with real
flour from real fields.

Dear friend, there is comfort in that. God was not asking Israel to
pretend. He received bread that looked like the bread on their tables.

The New Testament says something similar about us. We are living
stones being built into a spiritual house (1 Pet 2:5). We are still
being made holy, still under construction, and God receives us as we
are while He works on us.

Paul writes that we have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that
this surpassing power belongs to God and not to us (2 Cor 4:7). God has
never needed impressive containers.

You do not have to be finished to be offered. Bring what you actually
are to God today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I try to present a polished version of myself to God?
2. Can I accept that God receives me while still changing me?
3. What ordinary part of my life could I offer Him today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You receive me as I am and do not wait for me to
be perfect. I offer You my real, unfinished life today. Amen.
